# google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run

EvaluationRun is a resource that represents a single evaluation run, which
includes a set of prompts, model responses, evaluation configuration and the
resulting metrics.


To get more information about EvaluationRun, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.evaluationRuns)
* How-to Guides
    * [Official Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/evaluation/overview)


## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Evaluation Run


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run" "tf_test_evaluation_run" {
  region       = "us-central1"
  display_name = "eval-run"
  metadata     = jsonencode({
    tracker = "eval-tracker"
  })

  labels = {
    env  = "test"
    team = "evaluation"
  }

  encryption_spec {
    kms_key_name = "projects/my-project/locations/us-central1/keyRings/my-key-ring/cryptoKeys/my-key"
  }

  data_source {
    bigquery_request_set {
      uri            = "bq://${google_bigquery_table.eval_table.project}.${google_bigquery_table.eval_table.dataset_id}.${google_bigquery_table.eval_table.table_id}"
      prompt_column  = "prompt"
      rubrics_column = "rubrics"
      candidate_response_columns = {
        candidate = "response"
      }
      sampling_config {
        sampling_count    = 1
        sampling_method   = "RANDOM"
        sampling_duration = "1s"
      }
    }
  }

  evaluation_config {
    metrics {
      metric = "exact_match"
      computation_based_metric_spec {
        type = "EXACT_MATCH"
      }
    }

    metrics {
      metric               = "saved_metric"
      metric_resource_name = google_vertex_ai_evaluation_metric.eval_metric.id
    }

    output_config {
      bigquery_destination {
        output_uri = "bq://${google_bigquery_dataset.eval_dataset.project}.${google_bigquery_dataset.eval_dataset.dataset_id}"
      }
    }

    prompt_template {
      prompt_template = "Evaluate the following prompt: {prompt}"
    }

    autorater_config {
      sample_count    = 1
      autorater_model = "publishers/google/models/gemini-2.0-flash-001"
      generation_config {
        temperature = 0.2
        top_p       = 0.9
        top_k       = 20
        seed        = 42
        thinking_config {
          include_thoughts = true
          thinking_budget  = 128
        }
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [google_bigquery_job.eval_data]
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_evaluation_metric" "eval_metric" {
  evaluation_metric_id = "eval-run"
  region               = "us-central1"
  display_name         = "eval-run"
  description          = "An evaluation metric for EvaluationRun testing"

  metric = jsonencode({
    llmBasedMetricSpec = {
      metricPromptTemplate = "Rate the quality of the following response on a scale of 1 to 5. Response: {response}"
    }
  })
}

resource "google_bigquery_dataset" "eval_dataset" {
  dataset_id                 = "eval_run_dataset"
  friendly_name              = "test"
  description                = "Dataset for Vertex AI Evaluation Run test"
  location                   = "us-central1"
  delete_contents_on_destroy = true
}

resource "google_bigquery_table" "eval_table" {
  deletion_protection = false
  dataset_id          = google_bigquery_dataset.eval_dataset.dataset_id
  table_id            = "eval_run_table"

  schema = <<EOF
[
  {
    "name": "prompt",
    "type": "STRING",
    "mode": "NULLABLE"
  },
  {
    "name": "rubrics",
    "type": "STRING",
    "mode": "NULLABLE"
  },
  {
    "name": "response",
    "type": "STRING",
    "mode": "NULLABLE"
  },
  {
    "name": "reference",
    "type": "STRING",
    "mode": "NULLABLE"
  }
]
EOF
}

resource "google_bigquery_job" "eval_data" {
  job_id   = "eval_run_data"
  location = "us-central1"

  query {
    query              = "INSERT INTO ${google_bigquery_dataset.eval_dataset.dataset_id}.${google_bigquery_table.eval_table.table_id} (prompt, rubrics, response, reference) VALUES ('{\"contents\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"parts\":[{\"text\":\"Why is the sky blue?\"}]}]}', 'accurate and concise', '{\"candidates\":[{\"content\":{\"role\":\"model\",\"parts\":[{\"text\":\"The sky is blue because of Rayleigh scattering.\"}]}}]}', '{\"contents\":[{\"role\":\"model\",\"parts\":[{\"text\":\"The sky is blue because of Rayleigh scattering.\"}]}]}')"
    use_legacy_sql     = false
    create_disposition = ""
    write_disposition  = ""
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the Evaluation Run.

* `data_source` -
  (Required)
  The data source for the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_data_source).

* `region` -
  (Required)
  The region of the EvaluationRun. eg us-central1


* `metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Metadata about the evaluation run, can be used by the caller to store additional tracking information about the evaluation run.

* `inference_configs` -
  (Optional)
  The candidate to inference config map for the evaluation run. The candidate can be up to 128 characters long and can consist of any UTF-8 characters.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs).

* `evaluation_config` -
  (Optional)
  The configuration used for the evaluation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config).

* `labels` -
  (Optional)
  Labels for the evaluation run.

  **Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
  Please refer to the field `effective_labels` for all of the labels present on the resource.

* `encryption_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Customer-managed encryption key spec for this EvaluationRun. If set, this EvaluationRun will be secured by this key.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_encryption_spec).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_data_source"></a>The `data_source` block supports:

* `evaluation_set` -
  (Optional)
  The EvaluationSet resource name.
  Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/evaluationSets/{evaluation_set}

* `bigquery_request_set` -
  (Optional)
  Evaluation data in bigquery.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_data_source_bigquery_request_set).


<a name="nested_data_source_bigquery_request_set"></a>The `bigquery_request_set` block supports:

* `uri` -
  (Required)
  The URI of a BigQuery table. e.g. bq://projectId.bqDatasetId.bqTableId

* `prompt_column` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the column that contains the requests to evaluate. This will be in evaluation_item.EvalPrompt format.

* `rubrics_column` -
  (Optional)
  The name of the column that contains the rubrics. This is in evaluation_rubric.RubricGroup format.

* `candidate_response_columns` -
  (Optional)
  Map of candidate name to candidate response column name. The column will be in evaluation_item.CandidateResponse format.

* `sampling_config` -
  (Optional)
  The sampling config for the bigquery resource.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_data_source_bigquery_request_set_sampling_config).


<a name="nested_data_source_bigquery_request_set_sampling_config"></a>The `sampling_config` block supports:

* `sampling_count` -
  (Optional)
  The total number of logged data to import. If available data is less than the sampling count, all data will be imported. Default is 100.

* `sampling_method` -
  (Optional)
  The sampling method to use.
  Possible values are: `RANDOM`.

* `sampling_duration` -
  (Optional)
  How long to wait before sampling data from the BigQuery table. If not specified, defaults to 0.

<a name="nested_inference_configs"></a>The `inference_configs` block supports:

* `candidate` - (Required) The identifier for this object. Format specified above.

* `model` -
  (Optional)
  The fully qualified name of the publisher model or endpoint to use. Anthropic and Llama third-party models are also supported through Model Garden. Publisher model format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/*/models/*` Third-party model formats: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/anthropic/models/{model}` or `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/llama/models/{model}` Endpoint format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/endpoints/{endpoint}`

* `generation_config` -
  (Optional)
  Generation config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_generation_config).

* `agents` -
  (Optional)
  Contains the static configurations for each agent in the system. Key: agent_id (matches the `author` field in events). Value: The static configuration of the agent.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agents).

* `agent_run_config` -
  (Optional)
  Agent run config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config).

* `prompt_template` -
  (Optional)
  The prompt template used for inference. The values for variables in the prompt template are defined in EvaluationItem.EvaluationPrompt.PromptTemplateData.values. If not specified, the prompt template in the EvaluationConfig will be used.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_prompt_template).

* `parallelism` -
  (Optional)
  The parallelism of the evaluation run for the inference step. If not specified, the default parallelism will be used.


<a name="nested_inference_configs_generation_config"></a>The `generation_config` block supports:

* `temperature` -
  (Optional)
  Controls the randomness of predictions.

* `top_p` -
  (Optional)
  If specified, nucleus sampling will be used.

* `top_k` -
  (Optional)
  If specified, top-k sampling will be used.

* `candidate_count` -
  (Optional)
  Number of candidates to generate.

* `max_output_tokens` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum number of output tokens to generate per message.

* `stop_sequences` -
  (Optional)
  Stop sequences.

* `response_logprobs` -
  (Optional)
  If true, export the logprobs results in response.

* `logprobs` -
  (Optional)
  Logit probabilities.

* `presence_penalty` -
  (Optional)
  Positive penalties.

* `frequency_penalty` -
  (Optional)
  Frequency penalties.

* `seed` -
  (Optional)
  Seed.

* `response_mime_type` -
  (Optional)
  Output response mimetype of the generated candidate text. Supported mimetype: - `text/plain`: (default) Text output. - `application/json`: JSON response in the candidates. The model needs to be prompted to output the appropriate response type, otherwise the behavior is undefined. This is a preview feature.

* `response_schema` -
  (Optional)
  The `Schema` object allows the definition of input and output data types. These types can be objects, but also primitives and arrays. Represents a select subset of an OpenAPI 3.0 schema object. If set, a compatible response_mime_type must also be set. Compatible mimetypes: `application/json`: Schema for JSON response.

* `response_json_schema` -
  (Optional)
  Output schema of the generated response. This is an alternative to `response_schema` that accepts JSON Schema. If set, `response_schema` must be omitted, but `response_mime_type` is required.

* `routing_config` -
  (Optional)
  Routing configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config).

* `thinking_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for thinking features. An error will be returned if this field is set for models that don't support thinking.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_generation_config_thinking_config).


<a name="nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config"></a>The `routing_config` block supports:

* `auto_mode` -
  (Optional)
  In this mode, the model will be routed to the best model automatically.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config_auto_mode).

* `manual_mode` -
  (Optional)
  In this mode, the model will be routed to the specified model.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config_manual_mode).


<a name="nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config_auto_mode"></a>The `auto_mode` block supports:

* `model_routing_preference` -
  (Optional)
  The model routing preference.
  Possible values are: `UNKNOWN`, `PRIORITIZE_QUALITY`, `BALANCED`, `PRIORITIZE_COST`.

<a name="nested_inference_configs_generation_config_routing_config_manual_mode"></a>The `manual_mode` block supports:

* `model_name` -
  (Optional)
  The model name to use.

<a name="nested_inference_configs_generation_config_thinking_config"></a>The `thinking_config` block supports:

* `include_thoughts` -
  (Optional)
  Indicates whether to include thoughts in the response. If true, thoughts are returned only when available.

* `thinking_budget` -
  (Optional)
  Indicates the thinking budget in tokens.

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agents"></a>The `agents` block supports:

* `agent_key` - (Required) The identifier for this object. Format specified above.

* `agent_id` -
  (Required)
  Unique identifier of the agent. This ID is used to refer to this agent, e.g., in AgentEvent.author, or in the `sub_agents` field. It must be unique within the `agents` map.

* `agent_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type or class of the agent (e.g., "LlmAgent", "RouterAgent", "ToolUseAgent"). Useful for the autorater to understand the expected behavior of the agent.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  A high-level description of the agent's role and responsibilities. Critical for evaluating if the agent is routing tasks correctly.

* `instruction` -
  (Optional)
  Provides instructions for the LLM model, guiding the agent's behavior. Can be static or dynamic. Dynamic instructions can contain placeholders like {variable_name} that will be resolved at runtime using the `AgentEvent.state_delta` field.

* `sub_agents` -
  (Optional)
  The list of valid agent IDs (names) that this agent can delegate to. This defines the directed edges in the agent system graph topology.

* `tools` -
  (Optional)
  List of tools: each tool can have multiple function declarations.

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config"></a>The `agent_run_config` block supports:

* `session_input` -
  (Optional)
  The session input to get agent running results.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_session_input).

* `agent_engine` -
  (Optional)
  The resource name of the Agent Engine. Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/reasoningEngines/{reasoning_engine} For example: projects/123/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/456

* `gemini_agent_config` -
  (Optional)
  Config for scraping a Gemini Agent via the Interactions API. The scraping service creates interactions against the agent and returns the resulting interaction traces for evaluation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_gemini_agent_config).

* `user_simulator_config` -
  (Optional)
  The configuration for a user simulator that uses an LLM to generate messages on behalf of the user.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config).


<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_session_input"></a>The `session_input` block supports:

* `user_id` -
  (Optional)
  The user id for the agent session. The ID can be up to 128 characters long.

* `session_state` -
  (Optional)
  Session specific memory which stores key conversation points.

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  Additional parameters for the session, like app_name, etc. For example, {"app_name": "my-app"}.

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_gemini_agent_config"></a>The `gemini_agent_config` block supports:

* `gemini_agent` -
  (Required)
  The resource name of the Gemini Agent.
  Format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/agents/{agent}`

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config"></a>The `user_simulator_config` block supports:

* `model_name` -
  (Optional)
  The model name to use for multi-turn agent scraping to get next user message, e.g. "gemini-3-flash-preview".

* `model_config` -
  (Optional)
  The configuration for the model.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config).

* `max_turn` -
  (Optional)
  Maximum number of invocations allowed by the multi-turn agent scraping. This property allows us to stop a run-off conversation, where the agent and the user simulator get into a never ending loop. The initial fixed prompt is also counted as an invocation.


<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config"></a>The `model_config` block supports:

* `temperature` -
  (Optional)
  Controls the randomness of predictions.

* `top_p` -
  (Optional)
  If specified, nucleus sampling will be used.

* `top_k` -
  (Optional)
  If specified, top-k sampling will be used.

* `candidate_count` -
  (Optional)
  Number of candidates to generate.

* `max_output_tokens` -
  (Optional)
  The maximum number of output tokens to generate per message.

* `stop_sequences` -
  (Optional)
  Stop sequences.

* `response_logprobs` -
  (Optional)
  If true, export the logprobs results in response.

* `logprobs` -
  (Optional)
  Logit probabilities.

* `presence_penalty` -
  (Optional)
  Positive penalties.

* `frequency_penalty` -
  (Optional)
  Frequency penalties.

* `seed` -
  (Optional)
  Seed.

* `response_mime_type` -
  (Optional)
  Output response mimetype of the generated candidate text. Supported mimetype: - `text/plain`: (default) Text output. - `application/json`: JSON response in the candidates. The model needs to be prompted to output the appropriate response type, otherwise the behavior is undefined. This is a preview feature.

* `response_schema` -
  (Optional)
  The `Schema` object allows the definition of input and output data types. These types can be objects, but also primitives and arrays. Represents a select subset of an OpenAPI 3.0 schema object. If set, a compatible response_mime_type must also be set. Compatible mimetypes: `application/json`: Schema for JSON response.

* `response_json_schema` -
  (Optional)
  Output schema of the generated response. This is an alternative to `response_schema` that accepts JSON Schema. If set, `response_schema` must be omitted, but `response_mime_type` is required.

* `routing_config` -
  (Optional)
  Routing configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_routing_config).

* `thinking_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for thinking features. An error will be returned if this field is set for models that don't support thinking.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_thinking_config).


<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_routing_config"></a>The `routing_config` block supports:

  (Optional)

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_routing_config_auto_mode"></a>The `auto_mode` block supports:

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_routing_config_manual_mode"></a>The `manual_mode` block supports:

<a name="nested_inference_configs_agent_run_config_user_simulator_config_model_config_thinking_config"></a>The `thinking_config` block supports:

<a name="nested_inference_configs_prompt_template"></a>The `prompt_template` block supports:

* `prompt_template` -
  (Optional)
  Inline prompt template. Template variables should be in the format "{var_name}". Example: "Translate the following from {source_lang} to {target_lang}: {text}"

* `gcs_uri` -
  (Optional)
  Prompt template stored in Cloud Storage. Format: "gs://my-bucket/file-name.txt".

<a name="nested_evaluation_config"></a>The `evaluation_config` block supports:

* `metrics` -
  (Optional)
  The metrics to be calculated in the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics).

* `output_config` -
  (Optional)
  The output config for the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_output_config).

* `autorater_config` -
  (Optional)
  The autorater config for the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_autorater_config).

* `prompt_template` -
  (Optional)
  The prompt template used for inference. The values for variables in the prompt template are defined in EvaluationItem.EvaluationPrompt.PromptTemplateData.values.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_prompt_template).

* `rubric_configs` -
  (Optional)
  The rubric configs for the evaluation run. They are used to generate rubrics which can be used by rubric-based metrics. Multiple rubric configs can be specified for rubric generation but only one rubric config can be used for a rubric-based metric. If more than one rubric config is provided, the evaluation metric must specify a rubric group key. Note that if a generation spec is specified on both a rubric config and an evaluation metric, the rubrics generated for the metric will be used for evaluation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_rubric_configs).

* `dataset_custom_metrics` -
  (Optional)
  Specifications for custom dataset-level aggregations.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_dataset_custom_metrics).

* `loss_analysis_config` -
  (Optional)
  Specifications for loss analysis. Each config can be specified for one metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_loss_analysis_config).

* `cloud_logging_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for exporting evaluation results to Cloud Logging.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_cloud_logging_config).

* `allow_cross_region_model` -
  (Optional)
  Allows the evaluation run to use cross region models. When this flag is set, the service may route traffic to other regions if a model is unavailable in the current region (e.g., to a `global` endpoint). If a fully-qualified model endpoint resource name with a different region than the run location is provided elsewhere in the run config, this flag must be set to true or the request will fail.


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics"></a>The `metrics` block supports:

* `metric` -
  (Required)
  The name of the metric.

* `metric_config` -
  (Optional)
  The metric config.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config).

* `metric_resource_name` -
  (Optional)
  The resource name of the metric definition.

* `predefined_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for a pre-defined metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_predefined_metric_spec).

* `computation_based_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for a computation based metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_computation_based_metric_spec).

* `llm_based_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for an LLM based metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_llm_based_metric_spec).

* `rubric_based_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for rubric based metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_rubric_based_metric_spec).


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config"></a>The `metric_config` block supports:

* `aggregation_metrics` -
  (Optional)
  The aggregation metrics to use.
  Each value may be one of: `AVERAGE`, `MODE`, `STANDARD_DEVIATION`, `VARIANCE`, `MINIMUM`, `MAXIMUM`, `MEDIAN`, `PERCENTILE_P90`, `PERCENTILE_P95`, `PERCENTILE_P99`.

* `metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Metadata about the metric, used for visualization and organization.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_metadata).

* `predefined_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  The spec for a pre-defined metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_predefined_metric_spec).

* `computation_based_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for a computation based metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_computation_based_metric_spec).

* `llm_based_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for an LLM based metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec).

* `custom_code_execution_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for custom code execution metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_custom_code_execution_spec).

* `pointwise_metric_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Spec for pointwise metric.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_pointwise_metric_spec).


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_metadata"></a>The `metadata` block supports:

* `title` -
  (Optional)
  The user-friendly name for the metric. If not set for a registered metric, it will default to the metric's display name.

* `score_range` -
  (Optional)
  The range of possible scores for this metric, used for plotting.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_metadata_score_range).

* `other_metadata` -
  (Optional)
  Flexible metadata for user-defined attributes.


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_metadata_score_range"></a>The `score_range` block supports:

* `min` -
  (Required)
  The minimum value of the score range (inclusive).

* `max` -
  (Required)
  The maximum value of the score range (inclusive).

* `step` -
  (Optional)
  The distance between discrete steps in the range. If unset, the range is assumed to be continuous.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  The description of the score explaining the directionality etc.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_predefined_metric_spec"></a>The `predefined_metric_spec` block supports:

* `metric_spec_name` -
  (Required)
  The name of a pre-defined metric, such as "instruction_following_v1" or "text_quality_v1".

* `metric_spec_parameters` -
  (Optional)
  The parameters needed to run the pre-defined metric.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_computation_based_metric_spec"></a>The `computation_based_metric_spec` block supports:

* `type` -
  (Required)
  The type of the computation based metric.
  Possible values are: `EXACT_MATCH`, `BLEU`, `ROUGE`.

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  A map of parameters for the metric, e.g. {"rouge_type": "rougeL"}.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec"></a>The `llm_based_metric_spec` block supports:

* `metric_prompt_template` -
  (Required)
  Template for the prompt sent to the judge model.

* `system_instruction` -
  (Optional)
  System instructions for the judge model.

* `judge_autorater_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for the judge LLM (Autorater).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config).

* `rubric_group_key` -
  (Optional)
  Use a pre-defined group of rubrics associated with the input. Refers to a key in the rubric_groups map of EvaluationInstance.

* `rubric_generation_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Dynamically generate rubrics using this specification.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_rubric_generation_spec).

* `predefined_rubric_generation_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Dynamically generate rubrics using a predefined spec.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_predefined_rubric_generation_spec).

* `additional_config` -
  (Optional)
  Additional configuration for the metric.

* `result_parser_config` -
  (Optional)
  The parser config for the metric result.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_result_parser_config).


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config"></a>The `judge_autorater_config` block supports:

* `sampling_count` -
  (Optional)
  Number of samples for each instance in the dataset. If not specified, the default is 4. Minimum value is 1, maximum value is 32.

* `flip_enabled` -
  (Optional)
  Default is true. Whether to flip the candidate and baseline responses. This is only applicable to the pairwise metric. If enabled, also provide PairwiseMetricSpec.candidate_response_field_name and PairwiseMetricSpec.baseline_response_field_name. When rendering PairwiseMetricSpec.metric_prompt_template, the candidate and baseline fields will be flipped for half of the samples to reduce bias.

* `autorater_model` -
  (Optional)
  The fully qualified name of the publisher model or tuned autorater endpoint to use. Publisher model format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/publishers/*/models/*` Tuned model endpoint format: `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/endpoints/{endpoint}`

* `generation_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration options for model generation and outputs.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config_generation_config).


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config_generation_config"></a>The `generation_config` block supports:

  (Optional)
  Controls the randomness of predictions.

  (Optional)

* `top_k` -
  (Optional)
  If specified, top-k sampling will be used.

* `seed` -
  (Optional)

  (Optional)
  Configuration for thinking features. An error will be returned if this field is set for models that don't support thinking.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config_generation_config_thinking_config).

  (Optional)
  Indicates whether to include thoughts in the response. If true, thoughts are returned only when available.

* `thinking_budget` -

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_rubric_generation_spec"></a>The `rubric_generation_spec` block supports:

* `prompt_template` -
  (Optional)
  Template for the prompt used to generate rubrics. The details should be updated based on the most-recent recipe requirements.

* `model_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for the model used in rubric generation. Configs including sampling count and base model can be specified here. Flipping is not supported for rubric generation.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_rubric_generation_spec_model_config).

* `rubric_content_type` -
  (Optional)
  The type of rubric content to be generated.
  Possible values are: `PROPERTY`, `NL_QUESTION_ANSWER`, `PYTHON_CODE_ASSERTION`.

* `rubric_type_ontology` -
  (Optional)
  A pre-defined list of allowed types for generated rubrics. If this field is provided, it implies `include_rubric_type` should be true, and the generated rubric types should be chosen from this ontology.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_result_parser_config"></a>The `result_parser_config` block supports:

  (Optional)
  Use custom code to parse the LLM response.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_llm_based_metric_spec_result_parser_config_custom_code_parser_config"></a>The `custom_code_parser_config` block supports:

* `parsing_function` -
  (Required)
  Python function for parsing results. The function should be defined within this string.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_custom_code_execution_spec"></a>The `custom_code_execution_spec` block supports:

* `evaluation_function` -
  (Required)
  Python function. Expected user to define the following function, e.g.: def evaluate(instance: dict[str, Any]) -> float: Please include this function signature in the code snippet. Instance is the evaluation instance, any fields populated in the instance are available to the function as instance[field_name].

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_pointwise_metric_spec"></a>The `pointwise_metric_spec` block supports:

* `metric_prompt_template` -
  (Required)
  Metric prompt template for pointwise metric.

* `system_instruction` -
  (Optional)
  System instructions for pointwise metric.

* `custom_output_format_config` -
  (Optional)
  CustomOutputFormatConfig allows customization of metric output. By default, metrics return a score and explanation. When this config is set, the default output is replaced with either: - The raw output string. - A parsed output based on a user-defined schema. If a custom format is chosen, the `score` and `explanation` fields in the corresponding metric result will be empty.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_pointwise_metric_spec_custom_output_format_config).


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_metric_config_pointwise_metric_spec_custom_output_format_config"></a>The `custom_output_format_config` block supports:

* `return_raw_output` -
  (Optional)
  Whether to return raw output.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_predefined_metric_spec"></a>The `predefined_metric_spec` block supports:

* `metric_spec_name` -
  (Required)
  The name of a pre-defined metric, such as "instruction_following_v1" or "text_quality_v1".

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  The parameters needed to run the pre-defined metric.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_computation_based_metric_spec"></a>The `computation_based_metric_spec` block supports:

* `type` -
  (Required)
  The type of the computation based metric.
  Possible values are: `EXACT_MATCH`, `BLEU`, `ROUGE`.

* `parameters` -
  (Optional)
  A map of parameters for the metric, e.g. {"rouge_type": "rougeL"}.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_llm_based_metric_spec"></a>The `llm_based_metric_spec` block supports:

* `metric_prompt_template` -

  Template for the prompt sent to the judge model.

* `system_instruction` -

* `judge_autorater_config` -
  (Optional)
  Configuration for the judge LLM (Autorater).
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config).

* `rubric_group_key` -
  (Optional)
  Use a pre-defined group of rubrics associated with the input. Refers to a key in the rubric_groups map of EvaluationInstance.

* `rubric_generation_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Dynamically generate rubrics using this specification.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_metrics_llm_based_metric_spec_rubric_generation_spec).

* `predefined_rubric_generation_spec` -
  (Optional)
  Dynamically generate rubrics using a predefined spec.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_llm_based_metric_spec_judge_autorater_config"></a>The `judge_autorater_config` block supports:

* `sample_count` -
  (Optional)

  (Optional)

* `generation_config` -

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_metrics_rubric_based_metric_spec_inline_rubrics_rubrics"></a>The `rubrics` block supports:

  (Optional)
  A type designator for the rubric, which can inform how it's evaluated or interpreted by systems or users. It's recommended to use consistent, well-defined, upper snake_case strings. Examples: "SUMMARIZATION_QUALITY", "SAFETY_HARMFUL_CONTENT", "INSTRUCTION_ADHERENCE".

* `importance` -
  (Optional)
  The relative importance of this rubric.
  Possible values are: `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, `LOW`.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_dataset_custom_metrics"></a>The `dataset_custom_metrics` block supports:

* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  A display name for this custom summary metric. Used to prefix keys in the output summaryMetrics map. If not provided, a default name like "dataset_custom_metric_1", "dataset_custom_metric_2", etc., will be generated based on the order in the repeated field.

* `aggregation_function` -
  (Required)
  The Python code string containing the aggregation function. Expected function signature: `def aggregate(instances: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, float]:`

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_loss_analysis_config"></a>The `loss_analysis_config` block supports:

* `metric` -
  (Required)
  The metric to analyze (e.g., "tool_use_quality"). This filters the EvaluationItems in the EvalSet to only those where EvaluationResult.metric matches this value.

* `candidate` -
  (Required)
  The candidate model/agent to analyze (e.g., "gemini-3.0-pro"). This targets the specific CandidateResult within the EvaluationResult.

<a name="nested_evaluation_config_cloud_logging_config"></a>The `cloud_logging_config` block supports:

* `project` -
  (Optional)
  Google Cloud project to write logs to. Defaults to the request project.

* `tracing_context` -
  (Optional)
  Tracing context for the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_config_cloud_logging_config_tracing_context).

* `resource_type` -
  (Optional)
  MonitoredResource type. Defaults to "global" if unspecified.

* `resource_labels` -
  (Optional)
  MonitoredResource labels to associate the log with. The backend will automatically inject project and location.


<a name="nested_evaluation_config_cloud_logging_config_tracing_context"></a>The `tracing_context` block supports:

* `trace_id` -
  (Optional)
  Trace ID being written to Cloud Trace in association with this log entry. e.g., `12345`, the numeric ID from the resource name. If a trace or span is being evaluated, this field should be populated.

* `span_id` -
  (Optional)
  ID of the Cloud Trace span associated with the current operation in which the log is being written. e.g., `7a2190356c3fc94b`. If a span is being evaluated, this field should be populated.

* `conversation_id` -
  (Optional)
  Unique identifier for a conversation (session thread), used to store and correlate messages within a conversation. The value corresponds to the `gen_ai.conversation.id` field in the OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes.

<a name="nested_encryption_spec"></a>The `encryption_spec` block supports:

* `kms_key_name` -
  (Required)
  Resource name of the Cloud KMS key used to protect the resource.
  The Cloud KMS key must be in the same region as the resource.
  It must have the format `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{key_ring}/cryptoKeys/{crypto_key}`.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/evaluationRuns/{{name}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the EvaluationRun. This is a unique identifier.
  Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/evaluationRuns/{evaluation_run}

* `evaluation_set_snapshot` -
  The specific evaluation set of the evaluation run. For runs with an evaluation set input, this will be that same set. For runs with BigQuery input, it's the sampled BigQuery dataset.

* `state` -
  The state of the evaluation run.

* `error` -
  Only populated when the evaluation run's state is FAILED or CANCELLED.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_error).

* `evaluation_results` -
  The results of the evaluation run. Only populated when the evaluation run's state is SUCCEEDED.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_results).

* `create_time` -
  Time when the evaluation run was created.

* `completion_time` -
  Time when the evaluation run was completed.

* `terraform_labels` -
  The combination of labels configured directly on the resource
   and default labels configured on the provider.

* `effective_labels` -
  All of labels (key/value pairs) present on the resource in GCP, including the labels configured through Terraform, other clients and services.


<a name="nested_error"></a>The `error` block contains:

* `code` -
  (Output)
  The status code, which should be an enum value of google.rpc.Code.

* `message` -
  (Output)
  A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the google.rpc.Status.details field, or localized by the client.

* `details` -
  (Output)
  A list of messages that carry the error details. There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.

<a name="nested_evaluation_results"></a>The `evaluation_results` block contains:

* `summary_metrics` -
  (Output)
  The summary metrics for the evaluation run.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_evaluation_results_summary_metrics).

* `evaluation_set` -
  (Output)
  The evaluation set where item level results are stored.


<a name="nested_evaluation_results_summary_metrics"></a>The `summary_metrics` block contains:

* `metrics` -
  (Output)
  Map of metric name to metric value.

* `total_items` -
  (Output)
  The total number of items that were evaluated.

* `failed_items` -
  (Output)
  The number of items that failed to be evaluated.

## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 45 minutes.

## Import


EvaluationRun can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/evaluationRuns/{{name}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{region}}/{{name}}`
* `{{name}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import EvaluationRun using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    name = "<-optional value->"
    region = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import EvaluationRun using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/evaluationRuns/{{name}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), EvaluationRun can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/evaluationRuns/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default {{region}}/{{name}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_evaluation_run.default {{name}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
